messages:
Amy (AE): Hey team — trying to close a POC with Skybox. They want a Dedicated commit for the POC: 3 months, mixed GPU pool (4x A100 + 2x H100 equivalent), autoscale with burst up to 2.5x baseline. Need: a clear pricing path (commit rate, burst surcharge, conversion to long-term commit), and Ops lead time. Can we get an approval path? cc @Sam (SE) @Cheng (Pricing) @Maria (DealDesk)

Sam (SE): Quick technical notes: the workload is chat + embeddings. Typical seq len ~512, and KV cache hits expected to be high. They'll want 100 concurrent sessions at peak, but typical qps ~250. Burst to 2.5x seems reasonable during demo spikes. Storage/ingest is standard. No special network peering asked yet.

Cheng (Pricing): Suggested commercial sketch below — rough numbers to discuss, not final. Pricing assumptions: base commit covers baseline throughput (1.0x). Burst billed as percentage surcharge on consumed GPU-hours beyond commit.
```
Baseline commit (monthly): 6x GPU-equivalent pool = $65k/mo (commit rate)
Provisional burst allowance: 1.5x free burst during POC (up to 100 GPU-hours/month)
Burst surcharge beyond allowance: $35/GPU-hour (H100 equivalency pricing applied)
POC discount: 20% off list for 3 months convertable to 12m commit with credit for unused POC commit up to 50%
```
Cheng (Pricing): Also note: H100 equivalence multiplier = 1.5x on ratecard for burst billing, unless we map to specific SKU pricing. If they want strict H100 instances, rate changes.

Maria (DealDesk): From approvals perspective — this is doable but we need DealDesk sign-off for the POC credit + the conditional conversion clause. Please add the exact clause language: how POC commitment credits apply on conversion and what triggers conversion (signed contract within 30 days after POC). I can queue a fast-track if the ARR/prospect size justifies.

Amy (AE): Skybox indicated ARR target ~ $1.2M if converted. They want an option to convert the POC commit into a 12m reserved pool with prorated credits. I can confirm they’ll sign within 30 days on conversion if terms are favorable.

Eli (Ops): Lead time notes: for Dedicated pools we need 7–10 business days to provision mixed GPU pool in their preferred region, longer if H100 inventory is constrained. Autoscale & burst config: we can enable provisional burst policy but need service-account and networking details (VPC peering if Private). Ops also requires a ticket with expected qps/concurrency to size autoscaler windows.

Bob (Legal): Two legal ask flags: 1) Data residency / logs during POC — need clarity if Skybox will push regulated data. 2) Termination & conversion language: if they don’t convert, what happens to POC credits? Maria — can you draft the clause? We prefer credits expire 30 days after POC to avoid open liabilities.

Amy (AE): Noted. I will ask Skybox about regulated data and confirm timeline. Maria, can you draft the conversion clause and a short SOW addendum we can attach to the POC quote?

Maria (DealDesk): I’ll draft a 1-paragraph conversion clause and a service SOW addendum. Proposed language (working): "POC Commitment Credit: Customer will receive credit equal to 100% of POC monthly commit applied to the first three months of a converted 12-month Dedicated commitment if a binding order is signed within 30 days of POC completion. Unconverted POC credits expire 30 days after POC completion." Will circulate in docs.

Cheng (Pricing): Two additional options for structure — pick one early so we can get pricing approved:
- Option A (Simple): Lower commit rate, higher burst surcharge (gives Skybox flexibility, reduces our baseline risk).
- Option B (Lock-in): Slightly higher commit discount, smaller burst surcharge, with mandatory conversion incentive.
Which do you want to present to the customer?

Amy (AE): Present Option B first (they prefer clearer economics and conversion incentive). If they push back, we can fallback to Option A.

ops-bot: :gear: Provisioning note — new dedicated-pool tickets require: region, GPU types & counts, expected sustained qps, expected peak qps, service account, networking. Please open ticket using /ops new-dedicated-pool and attach the SOW addendum.

Eli (Ops): When you open the ticket, tag me and include a preferred start date. If they need H100 within 5 business days, we may need an expedited allocation request — that requires DealDesk ok for surge capacity.

Maria (DealDesk): I can approve surge allocation for POC up to 2x baseline GPU-hours for the first 14 days if Sales confirms ARR & exec sponsor. Post-PoC surge needs Finance approval.

Amy (AE): I'll confirm ARR & exec sponsor today and get back. Goal: have commercial sketch + SOW addendum queued by EOD so Ops can start provisioning early next week.

Sam (SE): One technical ask to include in the SOW addendum: enable KV cache persistence across warm restarts for the POC pool — that materially improves latency in their chat flows. Ops/Eli — is that ok?

Eli (Ops): KV cache persistence is supported but needs config in the runtime profile and additional ephemeral storage sizing. Add to the ticket. No blocker.

Cheng (Pricing): I'll prepare final Option B numbers and a short justification note (unit economics impact + conversion credit calc) and drop in the shared Google Doc: https://docs.google.com/sheet/d/skybox-poc-pricing (will DM the link to Sales).

Maria (DealDesk): Once Amy posts ARR and exec sponsor, I can fast-track the approval and lock in provisional burst credit. Pls @mention me in the ticket.

Amy (AE): Thanks everyone — I’ll confirm ARR & exec sponsor by 16:00 PT, upload the SOW addendum request, and open the ops ticket. If we get Maria sign-off, can we get Cheng to bless the final numbers so I can present to Skybox tomorrow? :thumbsup:

Cheng (Pricing): Yup — once Maria confirms, I’ll sign off and timestamp the quote for audit.

Bob (Legal): I’ll standby for the SOW addendum to review the POC credit language. Quick heads-up: if they push for longer data retention or special export rights we’ll need an NDA/DP addendum.

Amy (AE): Will update thread with customer answers. Thanks all :rocket:
